title: Service Desk (SD)
subtitle: Enterprise ITSM Incident Management & SLA Automation Platform
description: Architected product capabilities for the Service Desk (SD) platform, establishing automated multi-tier ticket routing, SLA threshold timers, priority escalation rules, and end-to-end incident lifecycle visibility.
overview: Service Desk (SD) is an IT Service Management platform designed to streamline incident resolution, SLA compliance, and support ticket governance. As Product Owner and Business Analyst at IE Networking Solutions, I owned the product vision and functional breakdown, turning complex support processes into intuitive automated software flows.
challenge: Support teams were hindered by manual ticket assignment, unmonitored SLA breaches, and ambiguity surrounding ticket ownership across Tier-1, Tier-2, and Tier-3 engineering squads. Lack of real-time auditability hindered root-cause investigation.
solution: Defined comprehensive business rules for automated skill-based ticket routing and dynamic SLA countdown engines. Authored Functional Requirements Documents (FRDs) covering severity classification (P1 through P4), escalation triggers, and post-incident review workflows. Wireframed responsive customer self-service portals and agent triage consoles using AI prototyping.

architecture.problem: Manual ticket dispatch and untracked service level agreements caused high Mean Time to Resolution (MTTR) and customer dissatisfaction.
architecture.tradeoffs: Engineered automated rule-based ticket routing matrices and event-driven SLA timer hooks to instantly escalate unresolved incidents.
metricsDetail: Architected automated ticket routing matrices, severity scoring models, and escalation paths
Authored extensive PRDs and FRDs specifying edge cases, state transitions, and SLA timers
Designed intuitive triage interfaces and telemetry dashboards with AI prototyping
Facilitated sprint planning, user story acceptance testing, and QA validation cycles
Delivered operator standard operating procedures (SOPs), user manuals, and release notes

outcomes: Dramatically reduced ticket triage friction and eliminated unassigned support requests.
Provided real-time SLA compliance monitoring and transparency for service management leadership.
Equipped enterprise support teams with clean, purpose-built tools that scaled with user volume.
